newsitem.title: JAPAN: North Korea demands apology over border incident.
newsitem.headline: North Korea demands apology over border incident.

text.p: North Korea demanded on Friday that South Korea apologise for an exchange of warning shots at their tense border shortly before U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen visited the area on Thursday.

"South Korea should apologise for having obstructed the normal patrol work of the (North Korean) People's Army and endangered their lives and they should take steps that this will never happen again," an official Radio Pyongyang broadcast monitored in Tokyo said.

Seoul officials said that in the incident, South Korean troops on patrol within the Demilitarised Zone (DMZ) fired 10 warning shots after spotting a group of North Korean soldiers who had crossed the border line.
The incident happened about one hour before Cohen visited an area of the DMZ about 100 km (60 miles) west of the exchange of fire.
"South Korea has created extreme tensions in the area by their indiscriminate military provocation which endangered the life of the People's Army," Pyongyang Radio said.
"We cannot ignore the fact that this is repeatedly happening just when the head of the U.S. military (Cohen) is being induced by South Korea into their plans to invade the North," it added.
